faqs.question: Is there Personal Income Tax in Antigua?
faqs.answer: No, Antigua and Barbuda abolished Personal Income Tax (PIT) in 2016. Employees receive their gross salary minus only social contributions (Social Security, MBS, Education Levy).

faqs.question: What is the total employer burden?
faqs.answer: The total employer contribution is approximately 13.5% to 15% of gross salary, covering Social Security (9%), MBS (3.5%), and Education Levy (1%).

faqs.question: Can I hire expats via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they require a Work Permit. The EOR acts as the sponsor. The process involves demonstrating that no local candidate was suitable, though specific skill shortages (e.g., IT, specialized engineering) make approval easier.

faqs.question: What currency should we use for contracts?
faqs.answer: Contracts can be in USD or XCD. We recommend XCD for local staff to avoid exchange rate fluctuations affecting their take-home pay, or pegging the XCD amount.

steps.title: Data Aggregation
steps.description: Collect timesheets, attendance records, and variable pay data (bonuses, commissions). Ensure overtime is calculated at 1.5x for hours over 40/week.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculate gross pay. Deduct Social Security (7% capped at EC$6,500 earnings), Medical Benefits (3.5%), and Education Levy (1%). No PIT is deducted.

steps.title: Employer Contribution Calculation
steps.description: Calculate employer liabilities: Social Security (9%), MBS (3.5%), Education Levy (1%). Total approx 13.5% on top of gross.

steps.title: Payment Dispatch
steps.description: Disburse net salaries to employee bank accounts in EC$ or USD via local ACH or wire transfer. Generate secure digital payslips.

steps.title: Statutory Filings
steps.description: Remit contributions to the Social Security Board and Medical Benefits Scheme by the 14th of the following month to avoid penalties of 10%.

steps.title: GL Reporting
steps.description: Provide General Ledger files compatible with your accounting system (QuickBooks, Xero, SAP) for seamless reconciliation.

items.title: Filing Deadlines
items.text: Social Security and MBS remittances are strictly due by the 14th of the following month. Late payments incur a 10% surcharge plus interest.

items.title: No PIT
items.text: Since 2016, payroll is simplified by the absence of Personal Income Tax. However, correct calculation of social levies is critical.

items.title: Maximum Insurable Earnings
items.text: Social Security contributions are capped at monthly earnings of EC$6,500. Earnings above this are not subject to the 7% (employee) or 9% (employer) Social Security deduction, though MBS and Education Levy may still apply to full gross depending on specific interpretation.

items.title: Multi-Currency Support
items.text: Process payments in Eastern Caribbean Dollars (XCD), USD, GBP, or EUR.

items.title: Portal Access
items.text: Self-service portals for employees to view paystubs and tax documents.

items.title: Audit Reports
items.text: Detailed monthly reports helping you stay audit-ready for Inland Revenue inspections.

faqs.question: What currency is payroll paid in?
faqs.answer: Typically Eastern Caribbean Dollars (XCD/EC$). The fixed peg is roughly 2.70 EC$ to 1.00 USD. Paying in USD is possible but may involve conversion fees.

faqs.question: How is overtime taxed?
faqs.answer: Overtime pay is subject to the same social deductions (Social Security, MBS, Education Levy) as regular salary, provided the total doesn't exceed the contribution caps where applicable.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: There is no income tax, but bonuses are considered part of 'insurable earnings' for Social Security purposes up to the monthly cap.

steps.title: Enter Gross Pay
steps.description: Input the monthly gross salary in XCD.

steps.title: Check Caps
steps.description: Ensure Social Security is capped at $6,500 earnings.

steps.title: Deduct Levies
steps.description: Subtract 3.5% MBS and 1% Education Levy.

steps.title: Review Net
steps.description: The result is the take-home pay.

items.title: Social Security Cap
items.text: Social Security contributions (7% Employee) are capped at insurable earnings of EC$6,500/month. Any income above this does not incur further Social Security tax.

items.title: Medical Benefits Scheme (MBS)
items.text: MBS is charged at 3.5% of gross salary. While some sources suggest a cap aligned with Social Security, strict application often applies it to full gross. Check with local payroll provider.

items.title: Education Levy
items.text: Education Levy is 1% of gross earnings. This is a dedicated tax for funding education infrastructure.

items.title: No Personal Income Tax
items.text: Remember, do not deduct standard Income Tax (PAYE). Antigua abolished PIT in 2016.

items.title: Simplicity
items.text: Antigua's payroll is relatively simple due to the lack of progressive income tax brackets.

items.title: Accuracy
items.text: Always ensure the strict 14th of the month deadline is met to avoid 10% penalties.

faqs.question: How often are rates updated?
faqs.answer: Rates are typically improved annually. These rates reflect the 2025 schedule.

faqs.question: Does this include bonuses?
faqs.answer: Bonuses should be added to gross pay to calculate correct social security deductions, up to the cap.

heroData.title: Company Formation in Antigua and Barbuda
heroData.subtitle: Launch Your Entity in 1-2 Days
heroData.description: Fast-track your business setup in Antigua and Barbuda with our expert incorporation services. From Name Reservation to Tax Registration, we manage the entire lifecycle.
heroData.bestFor: Investors and businesses needing a permanent local presence or IBC status.

steps.title: Name Search & Reservation
steps.description: Conduct a search at the Antigua and Barbuda Intellectual Property and Commerce Office (ABIPCO). Reserve the unique name for 90 days. Fee: EC$50.

steps.title: Document Preparation
steps.description: Prepare Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Directors, Notice of Address, and Statutory Declaration. Requires a local attorney to witness the declaration.

steps.title: Submission to ABIPCO
steps.description: File duplicate copies of all documents with the Registrar of Companies. Pay the registration fees based on authorized capital. Processing time: 1-2 days.

steps.title: Certificate of Incorporation
steps.description: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation. This is the official birth certificate of the company, allowing you to open bank accounts.

steps.title: Tax & Social Security Registration
steps.description: Register with the Inland Revenue Department for a Tax ID (TIN). Register as an employer with the Social Security Board, Medical Benefits Scheme, and Board of Education.

steps.title: Business License
steps.description: Apply for a Business License from the specific relevant ministry if required (e.g., Ministry of Tourism, FSRC for financial services).

items.title: Local Limited Liability Company (LLC)
items.text: Best for local operations. Subject to 25% Corporate Income Tax. Requires 1 director and 1 shareholder (can be foreign).

items.title: International Business Corporation (IBC)
items.text: Ideal for offshore activities. Tax exemptions (often 0% CIT) for 50 years, total confidentiality, and no requirement to file public accounts. Requires a registered agent.

items.title: External Company (Branch)
items.text: A branch of a foreign parent. Must file annual returns and financial statements of the parent company.

items.title: Minimum Directors
items.text: One director is required. Can be an individual or corporation, of any nationality.

items.title: Registered Office
items.text: Must have a physical address in Antigua and Barbuda for service of documents.

items.title: Company Secretary
items.text: Appointment of a Company Secretary is not mandatory for private companies but highly recommended for compliance.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital requirement?
faqs.answer: There is generally no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a standard private company, making entry easy.

faqs.question: Can foreigners own 100% of the company?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is fully permitted in Antigua and Barbuda.

faqs.question: Do I need to visit Antigua to incorporate?
faqs.answer: No, the entire process can be handled remotely through a local registered agent or attorney.

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: Standard incorporation takes 1-3 business days after documents are submitted.

faqs.question: Is there VAT?

faqs.question: When are corporate taxes due?
faqs.answer: CIT returns are due by March 31st of the following year. Any balance of tax is payable by April 30th.

faqs.question: Are there tax holidays?
faqs.answer: Fiscal incentives including tax holidays of 5 to 15 years are available for approved investment projects, especially in tourism and manufacturing.

faqs.question: Does Antigua have double tax treaties?
faqs.answer: Yes, Antigua has tax information exchange agreements and double tax treaties with the UK, CARICOM members, and others.

steps.description: Clearly define the services to be provided. In MSAs, this is often broad, with specific details left to Statements of Work (SOWs).

items.title: Governing Law
items.text: Explicitly state 'Laws of Antigua and Barbuda' to ensure local courts have jurisdiction.

items.title: Force Majeure

items.title: Currency Clause
items.text: Specify the currency of payment to avoid exchange rate disputes later.

items.title: Consideration
items.text: Like all common law contracts, MSAs must have valid consideration (payment for services).

items.title: Capacity
items.text: Verify that signatories have the legal authority to bind the company (Directors/Managers).

items.title: Stamp Duty
items.text: Certain types of contracts may require stamp duty, though simple service agreements are often exempt unless used in court.

items.title: Notarization
items.text: Deeds and instruments transferring property must be notarized and registered.

faqs.question: Is English law applicable?
faqs.answer: Antigua's legal system is based on English Common Law. UK precedents are often persuasive in local courts.

faqs.question: Can we opt for foreign arbitration?
faqs.answer: Yes, parties can agree to arbitration rules (e.g., LCIA, ICC) and a foreign seat, which Antiguan courts generally respect.

faqs.question: Are e-signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Electronic Transactions Act, digital signatures are generally valid for commercial contracts.
